picked.t: Vietnamese man who buys whole lottery stack wins with all 160 tickets, takes home $1.4M
picked.body: To Ich Tuyen, owner of the Ngoc Quang lottery agency in Ca Mau, confirmed on Oct. 26 that the agency had sold the stack and paid out the prizes, local media reported. The stack held 16 tickets bearing 361620, the special-prize number drawn by the Hau Giang Lottery Company, and 144 tickets that each won a VND50 million consolation prize, Tuyen said, as reported by Tien Phong newspaper. After 10% tax, the man took home about VND35.6 billion, he said. In Vietnam's southern lottery, a ticket matching the special-prize number pays VND2 billion, while one that differs from it only in the first of its six digits wins a VND50 million consolation prize. At VND10,000 a ticket, the whole stack cost VND1.6 million. The winner, who has not been named, regularly buys whole stacks of tickets at the agency, Tuyen said, Thanh Nien newspaper reported. At the customer's request, VND2.6 billion ($100,700) was paid in cash and the rest by bank transfer. The agency had sold winning tickets many times before, but customers usually won only a few tickets each, he said. This was the first time he had seen a customer win so much. The man had ordered the stack online and paid in full, then asked the agency to hold all the tickets because he was busy. The agency contacted him on the afternoon of Oct. 24, after the results came out, to tell him he had won.

picked.t: 베트남, '아시아 최고 미식 여행지' 한국에 내줬다…월드컬리너리어워즈
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 대한민국이 ‘2026 월드컬리너리어워즈(2026 World Culinary Awards, 이하 WCA)’에서 '아시아 최고 미식 여행지(Asia’s Best Culinary Destination)'에 선정되며, 베트남의 타이틀을 가져갔다. 동남아 외 국가가 이 상을 수상한 것은 한국이 처음이다. WCA 조직위원회는 최근 자메이카에서 열린 제7회 시상식에서 ‘아시아 최고 미식 여행지’로 한국을 선정했다. WCA는 전 세계 음식 및 환대 업계 분야의 여행지, 레스토랑, 기업 등을 선정하여 시상하는 연례 행사로, 수상자는 소비자와 미식 분야 전문가들의 온라인 투표를 통해 결정된다. 지난 2020년 신설된 해당 부문은 그동안 싱가포르가 1회, 태국과 베트남이 각각 3회, 2회를 수상한 바 있다. 베트남은 지난해 해당 부문을 수상하기도 했다. 한국관광공사에 따르면, 한국은 길거리 음식부터 바비큐 전문점, 그리고 서울 외 지역의 특색 있는 향토 음식까지 다양한 미식 경험을 제공하여 방문객들이 전국 곳곳을 탐방하도록 이끈다. 이에 대해 한국관광공사는 “한국은 길거리 음식부터 고깃집, 서울 외 지역 향토 음식까지 다양한 미식 경험을 제공해 방문객들로 하여금 전국 곳곳을 탐방하도록 이끈다”고 설명했다. 한국관광공사의 ‘K-로컬 푸드 트립 가이드에는 부산 돼지국밥, 전주 비빔밥, 제주도 흑돼지 구이 등 다양한 음식을 소개하고 있으며, 안동소주 같은 전통주와 계절 식재료 등에 대한 정보도 담겨 있다. 한편 베트남은 아시아 최고 미식 여행지 타이틀은 내줬지만 이 외 부문에서 존재감을 이어 갔다. 베트남항공은 '세계 최고의 미식 항공사(World’s Best Culinary Airline)'로, 사이공투어리스트그룹의 미식 문화·진미 축제(Culinary Culture, Delicacies Festival)는 '세계 최고의 미식 축제(World’s Best Culinary Festival)'로 선정됐다.

picked.t: The journey through unexplored jungle to discover 2-ha sinkhole in Phong Nha - Ke Bang
picked.body: In 2023, while searching on Google Earth, Nguyen Van Uy, deputy director of Jungle Boss Tours and a member of the U.S.-based National Speleological Society (NSS), discovered the black spot in the forest in the Cha Noi - Khe Gat area, within the core zone of the national park. The low resolution of the image made it impossible for him to decide if it was a sinkhole. He tried to fly a drone to inspect the area, but it could only reach a maximum altitude of 500 meters and not clear a mountain in its path. Later that year, Kevin Ditamore, a member of the NSS, visited Phong Nha - Ke Bang and met with Uy. They were surprised to find that they had both noticed the same black spot, and suspected it to be a sinkhole or a cave entrance. After cross-checking, they confirmed the two locations were the same. Ditamore returned home, leaving further exploration on hold. In early 2025, with a drone capable of flying up to 1,000 meters, Uy and some American experts surveyed the terrain three times. Uy says: "The aerial images recorded the mouth of the hole right in the middle of the primary forest. I confirmed that it was a sinkhole." By April 2025, a 10-member team, including two forest rangers, set off from Da Dao pass on the Ho Chi Minh highway in Phong Nha Commune, Quang Tri Province. Carrying over 35 kg of gear each, they trekked into the jungle to locate a way to the sinkhole's mouth. The sinkhole lies deep within the primary forest in hazardous terrain with no established trails. Even the National Park rangers and experienced trekkers were unaware of a route leading there. Team members had to push their way through dense vegetation, branches, and sharp thorns that sliced through skin and drew blood. Jungle leeches clung to their legs, staining their protective socks with blood. Near-vertical cliffs forced the expedition members to cling to tree trunks, treading cautiously step-by-step to prevent slipping and falling. At the end of each day, the team pitched tents, prepared meals, and rested overnight. Meals consisted mostly of dry rations, and the members had to replenish its limited water supply from forest streams. However, with the area being dominated by limestone mountains, there are very few streams, leaving them with no choice but to endure severe thirst at times. Two days passed, but the opening of the sinkhole was nowhere to be found. The team often had to change direction on encountering rock faces or impassable brush. The rugged, uneven trail and dense tangles of vines made trekking extremely difficult and gradually sapped the team's strength. By the end of the third day, as the group split into three directions to search, one member suddenly spotted the sinkhole's opening beneath the forest canopy. It was far larger than what had appeared in the drone footage. Uy says: "Everyone burst into tears of joy. We were all panting heavily after scaling the steep slopes, but the excitement felt like discovering buried treasure. Despite being hungry and parched, nobody cared, everyone just rushed over to get a look at the sinkhole's opening." Lacking the necessary gear to descend to the bottom and with rations sufficient for only a five-day itinerary, the team decided to record the coordinates, return, and prepare for a major expedition. "All 10 members were experienced trekkers with mountain-climbing skills, but upon returning home, every single one of us was left with scars from being cut by the jungle vegetation," Uy says. Building on the findings from April 2025, a full-scale survey was launched from July 23 to 29. The 24-member expedition team included NSS experts, the Jungle Boss technical crew, forest rangers, and Ditamore. The expedition team carried 500 meters of specialized rope, protective gear, and food supplies, with each person carrying a 30-kg load. After trekking over 20 km through the jungle, navigating sharp cat's-claw limestone rocks and sheer vertical slopes, the members reached the sinkhole's mouth, pitched camp, and divided into two groups. One team rigged the ropes for the experts to rappel down and survey, while the other took care of logistical support. Every day, six experts took turns rappelling down into the sinkhole to examine the terrain, rock faces, and geological features. The remaining members cooked the meals, transported water, and managed the other logistical operations. The survey found the sinkhole spread over an area of 2.1 hectares in Compartment 8, Sub-zone 603, a strictly protected zone of the Phong Nha - Ke Bang National Park. It has an oval-shaped opening measuring about 190 meters long and 140 meters wide. Inside, the maximum length reaches 250 meters, with a width of 200 meters and a depth of 120 meters. A notable feature is that the rock walls expand outward from top to bottom like an inverted bowl. The interior of the sinkhole is wider than its mouth, forming a massive chamber.
